chunks: The right of the people under the protection [of Islam] (dhimma) is that you accept from them what God has accepted from them and you do no wrong to them as long as they fulfil God's covenant.

key_terms.الذِّمَّة: Protection covenant; the status of non-Muslims living under Islamic rule
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic; an honorific title for God

ai.seo_question: What are the rights of non-Muslims under Islamic protection according to Imam Ali's Risalat al-Huquq?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin expands the concept of *dhimma* beyond mere legal protection to a spiritual covenant, urging believers to mirror divine acceptance in their treatment of non-Muslims. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *adl* (justice) and fidelity to treaties (*ahd*), ensuring that social harmony is maintained through consistent observance of the agreed-upon terms. The prohibition of oppression (*dhulm*) serves as a practical safeguard for communal stability and religious coexistence.
